_note: Which node each control drives. This file says WHICH node and which input; the workflow graph says what value it holds now; object_info says what kind of control it is. All three are needed - see backend/descriptor.py. Adding a workflow to the UI is an entry here, not a page.
_source: Every z-image/* graph is one group of the owner's canvas file 'Z IMAGE 6.json', converted with scripts/ui_to_api.py --all-groups --activate. The group is the unit: one canvas file carries seven switchable modes, and each becomes a workflow here.

z-image-txt2img.name: Z-Image Turbo
z-image-txt2img.description: Text to image on Z-Image Turbo, with LoRAs and a face pass.

example.prompt: A half-human half-rabbit young woman standing in a sunlit ceramics studio. Soft grey-brown fur runs along her forearms and the line of her jaw, and two long upright rabbit ears rise from her dark hair, thin enough that the morning sun passes through them and lights the inner shell a warm translucent pink. Her eyes are amber with round human pupils, her expression calm and a little amused. She wears a heavy linen apron over a cream knit sweater with the sleeves pushed to the elbow, and pale clay has dried in streaks across her fingers and one cheekbone. She is turned three-quarters toward a north-facing window with one ear tilted back, as though listening to something behind her. Low morning light rakes across the workbench, catching airborne dust and the fine down on her face. Shelves of unglazed pots recede behind her into soft focus. The palette is warm and muted - oatmeal, terracotta, pale sage. Skin and fur both hold real texture: visible pores, individual hairs, the small asymmetries of a real face. Framed chest-up with clear room above her ears, as an unhurried portrait taken on a fast 85mm lens.

z-image-img2img.name: Z-Image Image to Image
z-image-img2img.description: Redraw an image you supply. Denoise decides how far it may stray.

example.prompt: Keep the pose, framing and composition of the source image and render the same young woman as half human, half rabbit. Give her two long upright rabbit ears rising from her hair, thin at the tips and warmly translucent where light passes through, and soft grey-brown fur along her forearms and jawline that blends into skin at the cheek. Her eyes become amber with round human pupils. Everything else stays as it is: the same clothing, the same light, the same background, the same distance from camera. Keep skin and fur photographic, with visible pores, stray hairs and a natural slight asymmetry, and let the existing light in the picture fall across the new ears as it falls on everything else.

z-image-controlnet.name: Z-Image ControlNet
z-image-controlnet.description: Follow the shape of a reference image - pose, edges or depth.
z-image-controlnet._negative: The graph feeds one Text Concatenate to both the positive and the negative slot, so there is no separate negative text to expose. Adding a control here would silently write into the positive prompt.

control_mode.label: Control Mode
control_mode._why: An ImpactSwitch index. object_info calls it an INT, correctly, and a spinner from 1 to 999999 is useless for choosing between pose and depth - only whoever wired the switch knows what each position feeds. Hence the override; the values are node 117's input1..input5 in order.

example.prompt: A half-human half-rabbit young woman in the pose of the reference, photographed on a rooftop at dusk. Soft grey-brown fur runs along her forearms and jaw, and two long rabbit ears rise from her hair, one upright and one bent at the tip, thin enough to glow warm where the last of the sun passes through them. She wears a cropped charcoal jacket over a white tee, and the city behind her is out of focus, its lights beginning to come on. Cool blue shadows against the warm rim light on her shoulders and ear tips. Skin and fur both hold visible texture. Shot on a fast 50mm lens, chest-up, with room above her ears.

z-image-inpaint.name: Z-Image Inpaint
z-image-inpaint.description: Repaint the masked part of an image. Mask it in ComfyUI's editor first.

image.label: Image + Mask
image._why: LoadImage returns MASK as 1 - alpha, so this graph repaints wherever the uploaded PNG is transparent. Nothing about the node says that - the same class loads a plain image elsewhere - so the mapping declares it and the control offers a brush.

example.prompt: Fill the masked area with two long upright rabbit ears rising from the young woman's hair, matching this photograph exactly. The ears are covered in soft grey-brown fur, darker at the tips, and thin enough that the scene's light passes through the inner shell and lights it a warm translucent pink. They sit naturally where the hair parts, with a few strands falling across the base, and cast soft shadows consistent with the light already in the picture. Match the existing grain, colour temperature, depth of field and lens character so the ears read as part of the original exposure rather than an addition.

z-image-inpaint-automask.name: Z-Image Inpaint (auto mask)
z-image-inpaint-automask.description: Finds what to repaint by itself - pick the parts, no hand masking.

example.prompt: A half-human half-rabbit young woman: soft grey-brown fur along the jaw and forearms, two long upright rabbit ears rising from her hair with warmly translucent inner shells, and calm amber eyes with round human pupils. Keep the pose, the framing and the light of the photograph exactly as they are, and keep every texture photographic - individual hairs, visible pores, natural asymmetry - so the result reads as one continuous exposure.

z-image-detailed.name: Z-Image Detailed
z-image-detailed.description: Text to image, then a tiled upscale pass over the result.
z-image-detailed._size: Size comes from the rgthree latent node's `dimensions` picker, which is one COMBO of preset resolutions rather than a width/height pair.

example.prompt: A close portrait of a half-human half-rabbit young woman, lit by a single window to her left. Soft grey-brown fur runs from her temple down along her jaw and thins into skin at the cheek; two long rabbit ears rise from dark hair, the inner shells warm and translucent where the light passes through. Her eyes are amber with round human pupils and a clear catchlight in each. She wears a loose oatmeal sweater. Every texture is photographic and precise: individual hairs at the hairline and along the ear edges, visible pores across the nose and cheeks, the faint down on her upper lip, small natural asymmetries between the two sides of her face. Colours are warm and low in saturation. Framed head and shoulders on an 85mm lens at f/2, with the far wall falling into soft blur, and clear space above her ears.

minimax-h3-txt2vid.description: Text to video with native stereo audio, generated jointly rather than added afterwards.

encoder_device.label: Text Encoder
encoder_device._why: Whether the 15.7 GB text encoder goes on the card. It cannot sit there beside the 19.5 GB UNet on 24 GB, so 'default' makes ComfyUI swap one for the other on every run; 'cpu' keeps the encoder off the GPU entirely and the UNet resident.

example.prompt:
[Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic. A medium shot frames a young woman who is half human and half rabbit, standing at a market stall before dawn. Two long grey-brown rabbit ears rise from her hair, the inner shells warm and translucent under a hanging bulb. She ties an apron behind her back, and one ear swivels toward a sound off-frame. [Shot 2] At 00:03.000, the camera cuts to a close-up of her hands setting out apples, fur soft along her wrists, before she looks up and (S1) says: <d>[English] We open in ten minutes.</d>

audio.label: Song
audio._why: Same hidden-state pattern as the prompt: the chosen file arrives as LoadAudioState, a JSON string naming a file in ComfyUI's input folder - which is what /api/upload returns.
audio._control: The graph holds no value here - the file lives in a hidden JSON state - so the usual test for an upload slot finds nothing and this rendered as a text box. `audio` rather than `file` because the node takes a start and a length as well, and picking those needs to be able to hear the file.

minimax-h3-director.name: MiniMax H3 Director
minimax-h3-director.description: A timeline of shots, each with its own moment and prompt, rendered as one clip.
minimax-h3-director._timeline: timeline_data on node 5 is the storyboard itself - 1681 characters of JSON written by the node's own visual editor in ComfyUI. It is deliberately not exposed: a textarea holding that is not an editor, and the graph's own value is a working storyboard to start from. Driving it properly means porting the timeline editor, which is its own piece of work.

prompt.label: Shot prompts
prompt._why: One prompt per shot, separated by " | ". Pairs with Shot lengths - three prompts want three lengths.

segment_lengths.label: Shot lengths (frames)
segment_lengths._why: Comma separated, one per prompt: "36,48,36" at 24 fps is 1.5s, 2s, 1.5s.

timeline.label: Timeline (JSON)
timeline._why: The node's own state, written by its visual editor. The overall prompt, the soundscape and the character slots live only in here, so it is exposed raw rather than left unreachable. Porting the editor is its own piece of work.

shift_video.label: Video shift
shift_video._why: Flow sigma shift for the video stream. H3 was tuned at 12; moving it far changes the character of the motion.

shift_audio.label: Audio shift
shift_audio._why: The same for the audio stream. H3's default is 3.

ref_image_size.label: Reference detail
ref_image_size._why: Only used with references on. 'match' scales them to the output size and is fast; 'max' keeps a 2048px short edge for identity and costs real time.

start_frame.label: Start frame
start_frame._why: Driven by the storyboard, not typed. Present so prepare_payload will deliver it - a param the mapping does not name is silently dropped.

flux-krea-gguf.name: FLUX Krea GGUF
flux-krea-gguf.description: The quantised build. Same pictures, far less VRAM.

example.prompt: A candid editorial portrait of a young woman who is half human and half rabbit, taken in a greenhouse in late afternoon. Two long rabbit ears rise from her dark hair, their inner shells lit warm and translucent by low sun coming through the glass; fine grey-brown fur runs along her jaw and forearms and blends into skin at the cheekbone. She wears a faded green work shirt with the sleeves rolled, and holds a seedling tray against her hip. Shot on a 50mm lens at f/1.8 from just below eye level, so the leaves in the foreground fall into soft blur and the humid light hazes the background. Muted palette of moss, rust and bone. Natural skin with visible pores and flyaway hairs, no retouching, the slightly imperfect framing of a photograph taken quickly.

flux-krea-dev.name: FLUX Krea Dev
flux-krea-dev.description: The full-weight build, for when the card can take it.

example.prompt: A studio portrait of a young woman who is half human and half rabbit, lit by a single large softbox to camera left and a weak fill on the right. Two long rabbit ears rise from her hair, thin enough that the key light passes through the inner shells and turns them warm pink; soft grey-brown fur runs along her jaw and the backs of her forearms. She wears a black turtleneck against a grey seamless backdrop. Shot on an 85mm lens at f/4 at eye level, sharp from the eyelashes to the ear tips, with the fall-off of a real softbox across her cheek. Neutral colour, deep shadow detail, visible skin texture and individual hairs, the honest look of an unretouched frame.

flux-krea-img2img.name: FLUX Krea - Image to Image
flux-krea-img2img.description: Redraw a picture you already have.

example.prompt: Rework this photograph so the same young woman is half human and half rabbit, keeping her pose, her clothing and the original light. Two long rabbit ears rise from her hair, their inner shells warm and translucent where the scene's light passes through, and fine grey-brown fur runs along her jaw and forearms, thinning into skin at the cheek. Keep the lens character, the depth of field and the grain of the original frame, so the change reads as something that was always in the photograph.

flux-krea-depth.name: FLUX Krea - ControlNet Depth
flux-krea-depth.description: Keep the depth of a reference picture.

example.prompt: A half-human half-rabbit young woman standing where the depth map places her, photographed in a cold stairwell lit from a window above. Two long rabbit ears rise from her hair, catching the hard top light along their edges; soft grey-brown fur runs along her jaw and forearms. She wears a heavy grey coat. Shot on a 35mm lens at f/2.8 from slightly below, the concrete behind her falling away into shadow. Cool desaturated palette, hard-edged light, visible skin texture and stray hairs.

flux-krea-openpose.name: FLUX Krea - ControlNet Pose
flux-krea-openpose.description: Keep the pose of a reference picture.

example.prompt: A half-human half-rabbit young woman in exactly the pose of the reference skeleton, photographed on a beach at first light. Two long rabbit ears rise from her wind-blown hair, one bent at the tip, glowing warm where the low sun passes through them; fine grey-brown fur runs along her forearms and jaw. She wears an oversized cream cable-knit over swimwear. Shot on a 35mm lens at f/2.8 at chest height, the wet sand behind her a soft mirror of the sky. Pale pink and grey palette, long shadows, real skin texture with sand on her shins.

flux-krea-normal.name: FLUX Krea - ControlNet Normal
flux-krea-normal.description: Keep the surface detail of a reference picture.

example.prompt: A half-human half-rabbit young woman, her form following the surface detail of the normal map, photographed in a dim workshop lit by one bare bulb overhead. Two long rabbit ears rise from her hair, the light raking across their fur and picking out every ridge and fold; soft grey-brown fur runs along her jaw and the backs of her hands. She wears a canvas apron over a dark tee. Shot on a 50mm lens at f/2 slightly above eye level, hard top light and deep shadow, warm tungsten colour, every texture from skin pores to worn wood clearly resolved.

The young woman with long rabbit ears begins seated with her head lowered, then rises and turns toward the window in one continuous movement, her ears lifting as she stands. Audio: a chair scraping back, footsteps on floorboards, a curtain moving.
Music: a slow piano figure, sparse.

minimax-h3-director-gguf.name: MiniMax H3 Director (GGUF)
minimax-h3-director-gguf.description: A timeline of shots, each with its own moment and prompt, rendered as one clip. Quantised build, for cards with less VRAM.
minimax-h3-director-gguf._timeline: timeline_data on node 5 is the storyboard itself - 1681 characters of JSON written by the node's own visual editor in ComfyUI. It is deliberately not exposed: a textarea holding that is not an editor, and the graph's own value is a working storyboard to start from. Driving it properly means porting the timeline editor, which is its own piece of work.

prompt.label: Shot prompts
prompt._why: One prompt per shot, separated by " | ". Pairs with Shot lengths - three prompts want three lengths.

segment_lengths.label: Shot lengths (frames)
segment_lengths._why: Comma separated, one per prompt: "36,48,36" at 24 fps is 1.5s, 2s, 1.5s.

timeline.label: Timeline (JSON)
timeline._why: The node's own state, written by its visual editor. The overall prompt, the soundscape and the character slots live only in here, so it is exposed raw rather than left unreachable. Porting the editor is its own piece of work.

encoder_device.label: Text Encoder
encoder_device._why: Whether the 15.7 GB text encoder goes on the card. It cannot sit there beside the 19.5 GB UNet on 24 GB, so 'default' makes ComfyUI swap one for the other on every run; 'cpu' keeps the encoder off the GPU entirely and the UNet resident.

shift_video.label: Video shift
shift_video._why: Flow sigma shift for the video stream. H3 was tuned at 12; moving it far changes the character of the motion.

shift_audio.label: Audio shift
shift_audio._why: The same for the audio stream. H3's default is 3.

ref_image_size.label: Reference detail
ref_image_size._why: Only used with references on. 'match' scales them to the output size and is fast; 'max' keeps a 2048px short edge for identity and costs real time.

start_frame._why: Driven by the storyboard, not typed. Present so prepare_payload will deliver it - a param the mapping does not name is silently dropped.

ltx-23-txt2vid.name: LTX 2.3 Text to Video
ltx-23-txt2vid.description: A clip from a prompt, guided by one reference picture that also sets the frame size.

image.label: Reference image
image._why: Sets the output width and height through ImageResizeKJv2, and conditions the video at strength 0.7. The canvas calls this group TXT2VID; the graph does not work without the picture.

example.prompt: A young woman who is half human and half rabbit stands at the end of a wooden pier. A low-angle medium shot frames her against an overcast sky. Flat morning light, a palette of slate grey and pale rose, wet planks and damp fur catching a dull sheen. She pulls her coat closed, then turns her head to the left as her long grey-brown ears swivel a moment behind the movement, and takes one step toward the water. The camera pushes in slowly and steadily throughout.

ltx-23-img2vid.name: LTX 2.3 Image to Video
ltx-23-img2vid.description: Bring a still picture to life, with sound.

example.prompt: The young woman with long rabbit ears from the reference image stands where she is. A medium close-up holds her at eye level. The scene keeps its own light and colour, warm and slightly hazy, with fine fur texture along her jaw. She breathes, blinks, and turns her face toward the light; her ears lift and rotate a beat after her head. The camera holds still with a faint handheld drift.

ltx-23-image-audio2vid.name: LTX 2.3 Image + Audio to Video
ltx-23-image-audio2vid.description: A portrait and a voice clip become a talking, singing shot.

audio.label: Audio
audio._why: LoadAudioUI keeps the trim as three inputs, so the one control is spread across them (see workflow_service).

example.prompt: A young woman who is half human and half rabbit sits in front of a microphone in a small padded room. A medium close-up frames her from the chest up at eye level. Warm low light, deep shadow behind her, soft fur catching the edge of a lamp. She speaks the supplied audio, her mouth matching every word, her long ears tilting slightly as she emphasises a phrase. The camera holds completely still.

ltx-23-flf.name: LTX 2.3 First and Last Frame
ltx-23-flf.description: Two stills, and the motion that gets from one to the other.

example.prompt: A young woman who is half human and half rabbit moves from the first frame to the last. A medium shot holds her at chest height. Cool interior light warms as she crosses the room, her grey-brown fur picking up the change. She rises from a crouch, turns, and walks toward the window in one continuous movement, her long ears lifting as she straightens. The camera tracks alongside her at walking pace.

ltx-23-vid2vid-prompt.name: LTX 2.3 Video to Video
ltx-23-vid2vid-prompt.description: Redirect a clip you already have with a prompt.

example.prompt: A young woman who is half human and half rabbit, in place of the subject in the source clip. The shot scale, angle and camera move stay exactly as they are. Her fur is soft grey-brown along the jaw and forearms and two long ears rise from her hair, moving with her head. The existing light and colour of the clip carry across unchanged. She performs the same action from beginning to end.

ltx-23-vid2vid-reference.name: LTX 2.3 Video to Video (reference)
ltx-23-vid2vid-reference.description: Redirect a clip, keeping a reference picture's look.

example.prompt: The young woman from the reference image, half human and half rabbit, performing the motion of the source clip. Her face, her amber eyes and her long grey-brown ears stay exactly as the reference shows them. The shot scale and camera move follow the source, and the scene keeps its own light, a warm key from the left against cool shadow. Her ears move with her head through every beat of the action.

ltx-23-outpaint.name: LTX 2.3 Outpaint Video
ltx-23-outpaint.description: Widen a clip past its own edges.

example.prompt: The scene continues past the edges of the original frame. A young woman who is half human and half rabbit stands at the centre, and a wide shot now reveals the room around her: bare boards, a tall window to the left, shelves along the far wall. The new space carries the same soft daylight, the same dust in the air and the same muted palette as the source. She stays still, her long ears turning slightly. The camera holds its original move.

ltx-23-edit-anything.name: LTX 2.3 Edit Anything
ltx-23-edit-anything.description: Change one thing in a clip and leave the rest alone.

example.prompt: Change only the subject of the clip into a young woman who is half human and half rabbit: two long grey-brown ears rising from her hair and moving with her head, fine fur along her jaw and forearms, amber eyes with round pupils. Everything else in the shot is untouched - the same framing, the same light, the same background, the same camera move - and she performs the same action through to the end.

ltx-23-prompt-relay.name: LTX 2.3 Prompt Relay
ltx-23-prompt-relay.description: A timeline of prompts, each taking over for its own stretch.

timeline.label: Prompt timeline
timeline._why: The node's own JSON: a list of {prompt, length} segments. Editing it as text is honest until there is a timeline widget.

example.prompt: A young woman who is half human and half rabbit walks through a city at night, filmed in one continuous take. A medium tracking shot follows her at walking pace. Wet asphalt, neon reflections, a palette of teal and sodium orange, fine fur along her jaw catching the light as she passes each sign.
example.timeline: {"segments": [{"prompt": "she walks toward the camera, ears upright, hands in her coat pockets", "length": 36, "color": "#4f8edc"}, {"prompt": "she glances left as a tram passes, her ears turning with the sound", "length": 36, "color": "#e07b3a"}, {"prompt": "she stops under a sign and looks up, the light warm on her face", "length": 24, "color": "#d9534f"}, {"prompt": "she turns and walks away from the camera into the crowd", "length": 24, "color": "#5cb85c"}]}

ltx-23-first-frame-styler.name: LTX 2.3 First Frame Styler
ltx-23-first-frame-styler.description: Restyle a clip's opening frame with FLUX 2 Klein before animating.

example.prompt: A young woman who is half human and half rabbit, restyled as a painted illustration: soft gouache texture, visible brush edges, flat warm light. Her two long ears and the fur along her jaw keep their shape exactly, and the composition of the frame is unchanged.
